comments.author: sirpalee
comments.body:
There were plenty of presentations of how it works, you don't need to reverse engineer it.

Hint it involves lots of hand placed waypoints and finetuned behavior. The exact tech behind it is not too difficut nowadays.

comments.author: connected_user93
comments.body: It should be pretty straight forward to describe the enemy AI system used in FEAR. The only questions would involve the methodology that was used to achieve it. Chances are the methodology they used was a compromise in terms of performance limitations. Because we don't have those limitations, you should be able to just take a shot in the dark and recreate it. It's nothing magic really - the enemies just hide, flank, return fire, etc. Even thinking about it now I don't really see a reason to reverse engineer it. Just create it.

replies.author: PM_Me_Those_
replies.body: Agreed. There are tons of games since it came out that use similar enemy behaviors. Halo has had enemies like this since the first or 2nd game. Enemies who can recharge shields just dip behind a wall or rock and let it come back up, etc. Has OP just not been playing shooters for the last 15 years?

There's already plenty of implementation docs out there around it and many games since then have put in their own variations.

comments.author: oof-plap
comments.body:
There are excellent breakdowns on the Fear 1 AI on youtube you can watch.

It's really cool, but it's not some black magic sorcery nor something that AI will replicate very well aside from at a "systems" level.

It's a amount of manual paths and waypoints on maps which trigger certain barks at the player which creates the illusion of intelligent AI making choices. It's really impressive (especially for its time), but at a systems level its not actually doing anything crazy unique.

The reason AI won't do a good job with it, is that it requires a lot of "perspective", understanding where your player is, what they're likely to be trying to do, how to get enemies to "notice" this behaviour or create triggers in your environment which dictate certain behaviour weights in the AI. You'll only do a good job with this by practicing at actual level design.

Some of the barks like "behind the table", "behind the chair" etc are just waypoints where the player stands which cause vocal AI barks.
